title: UNIT THREE: POLITICS, ECONOMY AND SOCIETY IN ETHIOPIA AND THE HORN TO THE END OF THE THIRTEENTH CENTURY (PART 2)
content:
ሰላም፣ ጤና ይስጥልኝ ውድና የተከበራችሁ የEthioFresh አባላትና ትልቁ ቤተሰቦቻችን! ❤️✨ እንኳን ወደ History of Ethiopia and the Horn (Hist. 1012) Unit 3 Part 2 Tutorial በደስታ እና በፍቅር በሰላም መጣችሁ! ዛሬም እንደተለመደው ዋና ዋና ነጥቦችን በቀላሉ እንቃኛለን። መልካም ቆይታ! 🚀

3.2.2. East, Central, Southern, and Western States

3.2.2.1. Bizamo, Damot, Enarya, and Gafat
• Bizamo: Located on the southern bend of the Abay River, opposite to Gojjam around Wembera. Founded in the 8th century AD with early connections to Damot.
• Damot: Strong kingdom expanding south of Abay, north of Lake Turkana, west of Awash River, and east of Didessa River. Motalami was a prominent 13th-century king.
• Enarya: Located in the Gibe region of southwestern Ethiopia. Royal clan: Hinnare Bushasho (Hinnario Busaso). Kingship was divine; the king (Hinnare-Tato) was secluded/sacred and communicated via an intermediary called Afe-Busho. Power rested with the Mikretcho (council), including Awa-rasha (spokesperson) and Atche-rasha (treasurer). Residences were at Yadare and Gowi. Aksumite King Digna-Jan led a campaign here in the 9th century with Orthodox Christian priests carrying tabotat.
• Gafat: Territory lay south of the Blue Nile River on the southwestern periphery of the Christian Kingdom, adjoining Damot. Rich source of gold. People maintained indigenous religion despite Christian evangelists. Paid tribute in cattle from six districts (including Gambo and Shat clans). Rulers bore the title Awalamo.

👉
1. ቢዛሞ (Bizamo): በአባይ ወንዝ በስተደቡብ (ከጎጃም ማዶ በወምበራ አካባቢ) በ8ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን የተመሰረተ መንግሥት ነው።
2. ዳሞት (Damot): ከአባይ በስተደቡብ እስከ ቱርካና ሀይቅ፣ ከሐዋሽ በስተምዕራብ እስከ ዴዴሳ በስተምሥራቅ የተዘረጋ እጅግ ኃያል መንግሥት ነበር። በ13ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን ታዋቂው ንጉሣቸው ሞተላሚ (Motalami) ይባላል።
3. እናርያ (Enarya): በደቡብ ምዕራብ አባይ ጊቤ አካባቢ ይገኝ ነበር። ንጉሡ (Hinnare-Tato) እንደ አምላክ ይታይ ስለነበር ከሕዝብ ተሸሽጎ በነጋሪው (Afe-Busho) አማካኝነት ያወራ ነበር። አማካሪ ካውንስላቸው Mikretcho ሲባል፤ አፈ ጉባኤው Awa-rasha፣ ተቆጣጣሪው/ገንዘብ ያዥ Atche-rasha ይባላሉ። በ9ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን የአክሱም ንጉሥ ዲግና-ጃን ታቦት አስይዞ ዘምቶባቸው ነበር።
4. ጋፋት (Gafat): ከአባይ ወንዝ በስተደቡብ የሚገኝና በወርቅ ሀብቱ የሚታወቅ ነበር። ሃይማኖታቸው ሀገር በቀል ሲሆን ለመንግሥት ግብር በከብት ይከፍሉ ነበር። የመሪዎቻቸው ማዕረግ Awalamo ይባላል።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Prominent 13th Century King of Damot: Motalami.
• Title of Enarya King: Hinnare-Tato.
• Enarya King's Intermediary: Afe-Busho.
• Enarya Council Name: Mikretcho.
• Title of Gafat Rulers: Awalamo.

😂 የታሪክ ቀልድ: የኢናርያ ንጉሥ Hinnare-Tato ከሰው ተሸሽጎ በAfe-Busho ብቻ የሚያወራው እኮ ጥንታዊው "Do Not Disturb" Mode ወይም የTelegram Private Account ስቲንግ ስለነበረው ነው! 😜


3.2.2.2. Muslim Sultanates

• Emergence: Established since the beginning of the 8th century along trade routes from Zeila into the interior.
• Shewa: Founded in 896 AD (283 AH) by Makhzumi Khalid ibn al-Walid, claiming descent from Meca.
• Fatagar: Founded in the 11th century around Minjar, Shenkora, and Ada’a. Hilly lowland area producing wheat, barley, fruits, and extensive livestock grazing.
• Dawaro: Located south of Fatagar between the upper waters of Awash and Wabi-Shebelle. Used a currency called hakuna for commercial transactions.
• Bali: High plateau separating the Shebelle River basin and Rift Valley lakes, south to Gannale Dirre River. Strong army of cavalry and infantry. Trade based on barter (cattle, sheep, cloth).
• Ifat: Ran from Afar plain to Awash River. Established by Umar Walasma (1271–1285), claiming descent from the Hashemite clan of the Prophet. Weakened and annexed Shewa after intervening in disputes between Makhzumite princes Dil-Marrah and Dil-Gamis. Agriculture included wheat, sorghum, millet, teff, sugarcane, bananas, fruits, and livestock. Khat was used for the first time as a stimulant in Ifat.
• Moqadishu: Established by Abu Bakr Ibn Fukura al Din Sahil c.1269.
• Other States: Arababani, Biqulzar, Dera, Fadise, Gidaya, Hargaya, Harla, Kwilgora, Qadise, Sharkah, and Sim.

👉
ከ8ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን ጀምሮ ከዘይላ በሚነሱ የንግድ መስመሮች ላይ በርካታ የሙስሊም ሱልጣኔቶች ተመሠረቱ፦
1. ሸዋ (Shewa): በ896 AD በመኽዙሚ መሐመድ/ካሊድ የተመሠረተ የመጀመሪያው ሱልጣኔት ነው።
2. ፈጠጋር (Fatagar): በሚንጃር፣ ሽንኮራና አዳአ አካባቢ በ11ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን የተመሰረተ ለግብርናና ከብት እርባታ የተመቸ ቦታ ነበር።
3. ዳዋሮ (Dawaro): በአዋሽና ዋቢሸበሌ መካከለኛ ተፋሰስ የሚገኝ ሲሆን Hakuna የተባለ የራሱ የገንዘብ መገበያያ ነበረው።
4. ባሌ (Bali): በፈረስና በእግር ጦር የሚታወቅ የነበረና የዕቃ በዕቃ (barter) ንግድ የሚጠቀም ነበር።
5. ይፋት (Ifat): በኡመር ወላስማ (Umar Walasma) የተመሠረተ እጅግ ኃያል ሱልጣኔት ሲሆን በሸዋ መኽዙሚ መሪዎች (Dil-Marrah እና Dil-Gamis) መካከል የነበረውን ግጭት በመጠቀም ሸዋን ጠቅልሎ ያዘ። ካቲ/ጫት (Khat) ለመጀመሪያ ጊዜ ማነቃቂያ ሆኖ ጥቅም ላይ የዋለው በይፋት ሱልጣኔት ውስጥ ነው።
6. ሞቃዲሾ (Moqadishu): በአቡ በክር ኢብን ፉቁራ አል ዲን ሳሂል በ1269 AD ተመሠረተ።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Earliest Muslim Sultanate: Shewa (896 AD/283 AH).
• Currency of Dawaro: Hakuna.
• Founder of Ifat Dynasty: Umar Walasma.
• First Region to Use Khat as Stimulant: Ifat.
• Founder of Moqadishu Sultanate: Abu Bakr Ibn Fukura al Din Sahil (c.1269).



3.3. External Contacts

• Early Contacts: Contacts with Egypt since 3,000 BC and South Arabian kingdoms before 1,000 BC.
• Decline via Arab Expansion: Rapid expansion of Muslim Arabs in the Near/Middle East and North Africa disrupted Aksumite trade routes and shipping lines.
• Relations with Egypt (Mamluks & Bishops): Egyptian sultans used the consecration and dispatching of Alexandrian bishops (Abuna) as a political instrument to extract concessions from Ethiopian Christian kings. Ethiopian kings countered by threatening to divert the Nile (Abbay) River.
• Religious Communities in the Mediterranean: Pilgrimages to Holy Land (Jerusalem) via Cairo created Ethiopian Christian communities in Egyptian monasteries, Palestine, Armenia, and Italian city-states.
• The Prester John Myth:
- A legend arose in Europe around the mid-12th century during the Crusades (1095–1291) about a wealthy and powerful Christian monarch named "Prester John".
- A letter addressed to European kings appeared in Europe in 1165.
- Europeans eventually identified the Christian Kingdom of Ethiopia as the land of Prester John to seek a military alliance against Muslim powers.

👉
1. ከግብፅና ከአረብ ሀገራት ጋር የነበረ ግንኙነት: ኢትዮጵያ ከ3000 BC ጀምሮ ከግብፅ፣ ከ1000 BC ጀምሮ ደግሞ ከደቡብ አረቢያ ጋር የንግድ ግንኙነት ነበራት።
2. የጳጳሳት ፖለቲካ: የግብፅ ማምሉክ ሱልጣኖች የኮፕቲክ ጳጳሳትን (Abuna) ለኢትዮጵያ መላክን እንደ ፖለቲካ ማ ማስፈራሪያ ይጠቀሙበት ነበር። የኢትዮጵያ ነገሥታት ደግሞ "የአባይን ወንዝ እንቀይረዋለን" በማለት ይመልሱላቸው ነበር።
3. የፕሬስተር ጆን (Prester John) አፈታሪክ: በ12ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን በመስቀል ጦርነት (Crusades) ወቅት በአውሮፓውያን ዘንድ "ፕሬስተር ጆን" የተባለ እጅግ ሀብታም እና ኃያል ክርስቲያን ንጉሥ በምሥራቅ አለ ብለው ያምኑ ነበር። በኋላም ይህ ንጉሥ የኢትዮጵያ ንጉሥ እንደሆነ በማሰብ ከኢትዮጵያ ጋር ወታደራዊ ህብረት ለመፍጠር መፈለግ ጀመሩ።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Ethiopian Counter-Threat to Egyptian Sultans: Diverting the Abbay (Nile) River.
• Origin of Prester John Myth: Circulated in Europe mid-12th century during the Crusades (1095–1291).
• Significance of Pilgrimages: Linked Ethiopian Church to Egypt, Palestine, Armenia, and Italian city-states.


3.4. Economic Formations

• Agriculture and Irrigation: Mainstay of the economy. Small valley wetlands were drained for dry season cultivation to provide essential grains before main upslope harvests.
• Soil Fertility & Teamwork: Practices included manuring, composting, spreading residues, fallowing, crop rotation, intercropping, contour plowing, and collective labor.
• Land Tenure System:
- Communal Land Tenure: Ancient system giving group rights to community members.
- Rist Rights: Birthright to land based on ancestral kinship or lineage in northern Ethiopia. Inherited generation to generation. Landowners were called bale-rist.
- Gult Rights: Conditional right granted by the central government to state officials/functionaries to collect tributes from bale-rists for their upkeep and the imperial court.
- Riste-Gult: Hereditary transfer of gult rights among elite officials.
• Handicrafts: Included metalworkers (weapons/tools), carpenters (furniture), potters, and tanners. Artisans were generally despised, marginalized, and socially degraded by ruling elites who preferred imported luxury items.
• Trade: Political centers doubled as major trade hubs with road networks linking interior regions to coastal ports. Protection of trade routes from robbers was a primary state responsibility.

👉
1. የመሬት ይዞታ ሥርዓት (Land Tenure System):
- ርስት (Rist): በየትውልድ ሐረግ እና በትውልድ የሚወረስ የመሬት ባለቤትነት መብት ነው (ባለርስት)።
- ጉልት (Gult): መንግሥት ለሹማምንቱ ከባለርስቶች ግብር እንዲሰበስቡና እንዲጠቀሙበት የሚሰጠው የሥልጣን መብት ነው።
- ርስተ-ጉልት (Riste-Gult): የጉልት መብት ለልጅ ልጅ በሚወረስበት ጊዜ የሚፈጠር መብት ነው።
2. እደ-ጥበብ (Handicraft): አንጥረኞች፣ ሸክላ ሠሪዎችና ፋቂዎች ከፍተኛ አስተዋጽኦ ቢያደርጉም በማኅበረሰቡና በነገሥታቱ ዘንድ ይገለሉና ይናቁ ነበር። ነገሥታቱ የሀገር ውስጥ ቴክኖሎጂን ከማሳደግ ይልቅ የውጭ የቅንጦት ዕቃዎችን ማስመጣት ይመርጡ ነበር።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Rist: Inalienable birthright to land based on ancestral lineage.
• Gult: Right to collect tribute/tax from bale-rist granted to officials.
• Artisans Status: Despised and marginalized despite economic contributions.


3.5. Socio-cultural Achievements

1. Architecture:
• Aksumite Stele: Total of 58 stelae in and around Aksum carved at Gobodara in the 3rd century AD.
- Longest Stele: 33m tall (14-storied), decorated on 4 sides, broken on the ground with pre-Christian symbols (disc & crescent).
- Second Longest: 24m tall (10-storied), taken to Rome in 1937 by Italian invaders, returned/restored in 2005.
- Third Longest: 21m tall (9-storied), smooth backside with no decoration at the bottom (still standing).
• Zagwe Architecture: Carved from softer sandstone, registered by UNESCO in 1978. Categorized into three types:
1. Cave Churches: Internal decoration inside natural caves (e.g., Bete Meskel).
2. Semi-hewn Churches: Detailed interior with roofs/walls attached to surrounding rock (e.g., Bete Denagil, Bete Debresina/Mikael, Bete Golgota, Bete Merqoriwos, Bete Gabri'el-Rufa'el, Bete Abba Libanos).
3. Monolithic Churches: Completely carved out from surrounding rock inside and outside (e.g., Bete Amanuel, Bete Giyorgis, Bete Mariyam, Bete Medhanialem - largest; Bete Giyorgis - most finely built cross-shape).

2. Writing System:
• Sabean Language: Boustrophedon alphabet (left-to-right & right-to-left alternatively). Earliest inscriptions date to 9th century BC, consonantal (no vowels, e.g., D’mt, RDM, RBH, LMN with title mlkn).
• Evolution to Ge'ez: Developed 26 consonant letters (abjad). Vocalized script arose by 1st century AD (seen in Wazeba's coins). Fully vocalized trilingual inscription of Ezana created c. 330 AD by adding vocalic diacritics under Christian influence.

3. Calendar Systems:
• Oromo Calendar: Astronomical observations of the moon and 7 stars (Urjii Dhahaa: Lemi, Busan, Algajima, Bakkalcha, Arba Gaddu, Walla, Besa). 29.5 days/month, 354 days/year. Linked to pillars found in northwestern Kenya (300 BC) and Waqlim (c. 900 AD).
• Sidama Calendar: Lunar rotation with 13 months (12 months of 28 days + 13th month of 29 days). Week has 4 days (Dikko, Dela, Qawado, Qawalanka). New Year ritual is Fiche Chambalala.
• Ethiopian Solar Calendar: 12 months of 30 days + 13th month of 5 or 6 epagomenal days (Pagume). 7–8 years gap with Gregorian calendar based on Annunciation calculations. New year starts 1 Meskerem (Enkutatash) / Sept 11 (or Sept 12 in leap years).
• Muslim Calendar: Lunar calendar of 354/355 days starting from the Hijra (622 AD). Dates marked AH (After Hijra) and BH (Before Hijra).

4. Numerals:
• Ge'ez numerals appeared early 4th century AD, influenced by Hebrew, Arabic, and Greek. Lacks characters for multiples of 100.

👉
1. ሥነ-ሕንፃ (Architecture):
- የአክሱም ሐውልቶች: በአጠቃላይ 58 ሐውልቶች ሲኖሩ ከጎቦደራ ድንጋይ ተፈልፍለው የተሰሩ ናቸው። አንደኛው (33m - 14 ፎቅ) የወደቀ፣ ሁለተኛው (24m - 10 ፎቅ) በ1937 በጣሊያን ተወስዶ በ2005 የተመለሰ፣ ሦስተኛው (21m - 9 ፎቅ) አሁንም ቆሞ የሚገኝ ነው።
- የዛጉዌ አብያተ ክርስቲያናት (1978 UNESCO): በ3 ይከፈላሉ፦
• ዋሻ (Cave): ቤተ መስቀል።
• ከፊል-ውቅር (Semi-hewn): ቤተ ደናግል፣ ቤተ ጎልጎታ፣ ቤተ ገብርኤል ሩፋኤል ወዘተ።
• ሙሉ-ውቅር (Monolithic): ቤተ አማኑኤል፣ ቤተ ማርያም፣ ቤተ መድኃኔዓለም (ትልቁ) እና ቤተ ጊዮርጊስ (በመስቀል ቅርጽ በተዋበ ሁኔታ የታነጸ)።
2. የጽሑፍ ሥርዓት: ከሳባውያን ጽሑፍ (አናባቢ የሌለው) ወደ ግዕዝ ፊደላት ተቀየረ። በንጉሥ ዋዜባ ሳንቲም ላይ አናባቢዎች መታየት የጀመሩ ሲሆን በ330 AD በንጉሥ ኢዛና ዘመን ሙሉ በሙሉ አናባቢ ያላቸው (vocalized) ፊደላት በሦስት ቋንቋ ጽሑፍ ላይ ውለዋል።
3. የዘመን አቆጣጠር (Calendar):
- የኦሮሞ ካሌንደር: በጨረቃና በ7 ኮከቦች (Urjii Dhahaa) ምልከታ ላይ የተመሠረተ (354 ቀናት)።
- የሲዳማ ካሌንደር: 13 ወራት ያሉት፤ ሳምንቱ 4 ቀናት (Dikko, Dela, Qawado, Qawalanka) አሉት። በዓሉ Fiche Chambalala ይባላል።
- የኢትዮጵያ ሶላር ካሌንደር: 12 ወራት የ30 ቀን + ጳጉሜ (5/6 ቀን)።
- የእስልምና ካሌንደር: በሂጅራ (622 AD) የሚጀምር የጨረቃ ካሌንደር (AH)።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Largest Zagwe Monolithic Church: Bete Medhanialem.
• Finely Built Cross-Shaped Church: Bete Giyorgis.
• First Vocalized Ge'ez Inscriptions: Ezana's trilingual inscription (c. 330 AD); early signs on King Wazeba's coins.
• Sidama New Year Festival: Fiche Chambalala (week has 4 days).
• Oromo Calendar Basis: Moon and 7 stars (Urjii Dhahaa).
